title: First Ellington recording, The Sheik of Araby
summary: His first Ellington session in New York was The Sheik of Araby, with Hodges also soloing, dated May 16, 1932 by the discography.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I want -- when did the group recordings really --
The first record I made was "The Sheik," in New York. What -- I'm trying to think of the director's name, the engineer's name. He later became very famous out here in the movies.
That was the first recording you made with Duke Ellington, right? "The Shiek of Araby"?
And that was, according to Benny Ansell's Agsland

(PHONETIC) Discribophy, May 16th, 1932. And according to the discography Discribophy (PHONETIC), again, on that same date, "Blue Harlem," was recorded. Just the two, "Blue Harlem," and "The Shiek of Araby," and you had a solo, you and Johnny Hodges had solos on "The Shiek of Araby."
But that wasn't the first time you recorded, that was the first time you recorded with Duke Ellington.
